input.summary: Meridian has 31 active programs across 24 use cases; all seven flagship initiatives are blocked by foundational evidence gaps.
covers: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM Automation
sources: MER-V3-EVID-PROG-* series (14 named program evidence refs)
Epic Clarity / Caboodle; Claims administration platform; SAS analytics estate; SQL Server reporting marts; Databricks on AWS (target)

story.meaning: Meridian's program portfolio is strategically coherent but operationally unready — every flagship use case is gated by the same missing foundations: no certified medallion architecture, no identity spine, no formal governance, and no AI audit trail.
story.observed: 31 of 256 program rows are active; 225 remain candidate. All seven CEO/CFO-priority use cases are in planning stage with open evidence gates. AWS/Databricks is the target direction but no certified platform foundation is evidenced.
story.matters: Without closing the lakehouse, governance, and contract-digitization gates, Meridian cannot advance any of its top-five use cases from planning to execution — stalling AI, cost transparency, and quality initiatives simultaneously.
story.supports: Resolve the five evidence gates in priority order: (1) lakehouse foundation, (2) data governance operating model, (3) provider contract digitization, (4) transcript governance, (5) payment integrity model lineage.

findings: All seven flagship programs share a common blocker: no certified medallion architecture and no formal data governance operating model — resolving these two gates unblocks the entire portfolio.

225 of 256 program rows remain candidate status, signaling that Meridian's initiative inventory is aspirational; active program count (31) is insufficient to cover the breadth of stated strategic priorities.

Payment integrity and cost transparency are the CFO's top-cited value levers, yet both are blocked by ungoverned SAS model lineage and undigitized provider contract terms — neither gap has an assigned owner or timeline.

Call center optimization spans Genesys, Salesforce Health Cloud, and the claims platform but lacks transcript governance, real-time integration proof, and member identity linkage — three prerequisites that must be sequenced before any agent-assist value can be measured.

relationships.note: The programs dimension is the strategic demand layer. Its execution is entirely contingent on the platform and governance dimensions closing their evidence gates first — making programs the leading indicator of portfolio risk, not portfolio progress.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture or patient/member identity spine
gaps.blocks: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse — the foundational program for four downstream use cases
gaps.needed: Epic Clarity medallion build, claims/pharmacy harmonization proof, AWS/Databricks foundation certification
gaps.handoff: Assign platform engineering owner; require architecture sign-off before lakehouse program advances to execution

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model and no certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: All AI/LLM automation programs; also blocks cost transparency, quality, and payment integrity
gaps.needed: Domain stewardship assignments, data quality rule evidence, AI audit trail, certified semantic layer
gaps.handoff: CDAO to own governance operating model; gate all AI program activations on governance certification

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form; attribution ownership unproven
gaps.blocks: End-to-End Cost Transparency and Provider Quality and Performance programs
gaps.needed: Contract digitization project, GL/claims calendar alignment proof, margin semantic model certification
gaps.handoff: CFO and Network Contracting to co-own; require finance/actuarial baseline signoff before value claims

gaps.blocks: Call Center Optimization — agent-assist and next-best-action cannot be measured without these

gaps.handoff: Chief Experience Officer to own baseline AHT/FCR/containment data capture before program advances

gaps.missing: SAS payment integrity model lineage ungoverned; recovery workflow and provider entity resolution unproven
gaps.blocks: Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction — leakage quantification is not possible without these
gaps.needed: SAS model lineage governance, provider entity resolution certification, investigation and recovery tracking
gaps.handoff: CFO and Health Plan Ops to assign recovery workflow owner; finance must validate recoveries before value is claimed

evidence.name: Programs & Initiatives Master Dataset
evidence.facts: 24 distinct use cases catalogued; 7 CEO/CFO-priority programs all in planning stage; confidence split 188 high / 68 medium
evidence.fields: business_name, use_case, data_domain, systems, value_hypothesis, evidence_needed, active_candidate_status, confidence
evidence.supports: Portfolio scope, active vs. candidate split, use-case-to-system mapping, and evidence gate inventory
evidence.missing: Program owners not populated; no budget or timeline fields; no milestone or stage-gate dates evidenced

evidence.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active program rows (EMR clinical, claims, pharmacy)
evidence.facts: All three rows blocked by same four gates: no medallion architecture, no identity spine, claims/pharmacy harmonization unproven, AWS/Databricks foundation not ready
evidence.supports: Confirms lakehouse is the foundational prerequisite program; no platform readiness evidence exists
evidence.missing: No Epic Clarity medallion build plan; no identity spine load evidence; no AWS/Databricks certification

evidence.name: AI / LLM Automation Governance Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active program rows (prior auth, coding, utilization management)
evidence.facts: No formal governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, no AI audit trail, no data quality rules — all four gates open across all three rows
evidence.supports: Governance gap is the single largest cross-portfolio blocker; affects all AI/LLM programs
evidence.missing: No domain steward assignments; no audit trail design; no semantic layer certification timeline

evidence.name: Payment Integrity and Cost Transparency Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 6 active program rows across payment integrity (3) and cost transparency (3)
evidence.facts: SAS model lineage ungoverned; provider contracts not digitized; GL/claims calendar alignment unproven; recovery tracking absent
evidence.supports: CFO's top two value levers are both blocked by the same contract and lineage governance gaps
evidence.missing: No recovery workflow owner; no finance-validated baseline; no provider entity resolution proof

evidence.name: Call Center Optimization Evidence Bundle
evidence.rows: 3 active program rows (transcripts, CRM cases, claims status)
evidence.facts: Transcript governance absent; real-time Genesys-to-Salesforce integration unproven; intent taxonomy not certified; member identity linkage not proven
evidence.supports: Agent-assist and next-best-action programs cannot be measured without baseline AHT, FCR, and containment data
evidence.missing: No AHT/FCR/CSAT baseline loaded; no real-time integration architecture evidenced; no QA-label governance

evidence.name: Stakeholder Interview Evidence Series (SA07)
evidence.facts: CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, CMO, Chief Experience Officer all independently cite lakehouse, governance, cost transparency, and call center as top priorities; no stakeholder cited a completed evidence gate
evidence.fields: Stakeholder role, priority alignment, program citation, evidence gate acknowledgment
evidence.supports: Confirms cross-executive alignment on program priorities; also confirms universal awareness that foundations are not yet in place
evidence.missing: No executive has been assigned as accountable owner for any specific evidence gate closure
